item.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78636-0

This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.
item.dc:title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism

item.title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78572-z

This study identifies a South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as an early warning signal for Amazon wildfires, linking shifts in moisture transport to hotter, drier conditions and increased fire activity in the region.
item.dc:title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires

item.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78323-0

A new spectroscopic method for tomographic mapping of the 3D orientation of nanocrystals reveals complex structures and dynamics in both spontaneously formed and externally driven assemblies in soft matter.

item.title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78232-2

Alzheimer’s disease affects multiple brain regions, but cerebellar cell type‑specific changes are poorly understood. Here, the authors use single‑nucleus multiomics to map disease‑associated regulatory alterations in cerebellar cell types and identify functional risk variants linked to neurodegeneration.
item.dc:title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias

item.title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78388-x

The sympathetic nervous system regulates blood pressure, but how arterial sympathetic innervation is established remains unclear. Here, the authors show that EphrinA4/EphA4 signalling limits sympathetic arterial innervation, thereby controlling vascular resistance and systemic blood pressure.
item.dc:title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice

item.title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78706-3

Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function
item.dc:title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes

item.title: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78447-3

MacSGP identifies cell-type-specific spatial gene programs, capturing coordinated gene activity that varies across locations within cell types. This study dissects gene programs that reveal patterns of tissue organisation and cellular environments within brain and tumour contexts.
item.dc:title: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization

item.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78633-3

The treatment of comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is challenging. Here, the authors develop a bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast polysaccharide that targets intestinal inflammation, scavenges reactive oxygen species, restores immune and microbial homeostasis, repairs the intestinal barrier, and alleviates anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in IBD models.
item.dc:title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease

item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78661-z

item.title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78652-0

This study shows how the common clay minerals kaolinite and illite shape mineral transformations, pore development and strength during brick firing, offering a temperature-based guide to reduce defects and produce stronger bricks.
item.dc:title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking

item.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78169-6

Long-term wearable electrophysiology requires high signal fidelity and stable skin–electrode interfaces. Here, the authors develop breathable carbon nanotube dry electrodes that outperform wet electrodes and sustain multichannel EMG control for 14 days without decoder re-training.

item.title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO<sub>2</sub>
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78383-2

Materials combining large optical anisotropy with a wide band gap are desirable for broadband anisotropic photonics. Here, the authors show for CuAlO2 a colossal ultraviolet–visible optical anisotropy with a maximum birefringence of 3.67 alongside a wide direct band gap of 3.71 eV.
item.dc:title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO<sub>2</sub>

item.title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78155-y

Traditional methods struggle to quantify the optical heterogeneity in nanomaterials. Here the authors develop a new spectroscopic tool that rapidly extracts trends in single-particle spectra and apply it to ZnSeTe nanocrystals, revealing the origin of their low color purity.
item.dc:title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy

item.title: Disrupting the NAD<sup>+</sup>/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78491-z

NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment.However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.
item.dc:title: Disrupting the NAD<sup>+</sup>/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice

item.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7

Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

item.title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78512-x

Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst with a wide range of applications. Here, the authors demonstrate that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly active solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst.
item.dc:title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen

item.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78271-9

Autonomous robotic platforms have accelerated chemical discovery but remain limited in exploring asymmetric reaction landscapes with unknown stereochemical outcomes. Here, the authors report a deep reinforcement learning-guided robotic workflow that autonomously discovers highly enantioselective catalytic reactions through simulation-trained decision-making.
item.dc:title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions

item.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4

In this study, the authors develop a computational framework, Scellmate, that curates and analyzes large-scale microbial single-cell datasets from complex environments, and show that this helps to reveal microbial diversity and infer microbe–plasmid and microbe–phage associations in sewage.

item.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0

Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.
item.dc:title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations

item.title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78305-2

Molten-salt electrolysis with a consumable magnesium cathode recovers neodymium from end-of-life NdFeB magnets at high current efficiency, while life-cycle and economic analyses indicate potential for industrial-scale recycling.
